# Choose tree depth before final evaluation

Complete `choose_depth(scores)` in `exercise.py`. Its input is a
nonempty dictionary mapping integer depths 0 through 8 to finite validation
accuracies from 0 to 1. Return the shallowest depth within 0.02 of the best
accuracy, with an inclusive boundary and `1e-12` numerical tolerance.
Reject values outside this contract with `ValueError`.

For `{0:0.5,1:0.75,2:1.0}`, select 2. For
`{2:1.0,1:0.98}`, select 1. An exact accuracy tie also selects the
shallower candidate. Explain the declared simplicity preference before
running the experiment.

## Supplied experiment

Both roles contain `main.py`, `exercise.py`, `tree_rules.py`,
source notes and separate training, validation and test CSVs. Use Python
3.10 or later and its standard library:

```sh
python3 main.py --output tree-report.json
```

Keep those files and the `data` folder together. CSV paths are relative
to `main.py`; an absolute path to that script also works from another
folder. The untouched starter stops at `choose_depth`. Complete that
function, save the project and reopen it before exporting the full ZIP.

The supplied code fits depths 0,1,2 on the eight training rows, scores the
four validation rows, calls the selection function, then opens the four
test rows. It keeps training alone for fitting throughout this exercise.

## Worked result and interpretation

The [worked lab](#machine-learning-ml3-5-decision-trees-and-interpretable-models-curriculum-decision-tree-lab)
gives every input, fitted count and comparison. Expect validation accuracies
0.5,0.75,1.0 and selected depth 2. Final predictions A,A,B,A score 1.0;
the training-only majority baseline scores 0.75.

Inspect `tree-report.json` for candidate scores, chosen depth, the
complete fitted tree, final predictions, baseline and each test path.
Trace x=7.5 through comparisons with 1.5 and 5.5 to its A leaf. Explain the
mixed B leaf that would stop that query in the depth-1 tree.

In a separate saved copy, change only one final-test label. Candidate
scores, chosen depth, fitted counts and predictions must remain unchanged;
final accuracy may change. Explain why selecting depth from those labels
would turn the final test into another tuning opportunity.

Retain the report, one hand-traced prediction and the comparison with the
same-row baseline. The fixture is a reproducible teaching example. A perfect
score on these four authored rows supplies no population-performance claim.

ML35-Decision-Tree-Selection/starter/SOU.content:
# Source and data

This authored course exercise reuses the complete bounded tree rules from
AI-Level-2 commit `609c914d179ffde8518cfbfdb74f6739f9a0418d`,
`ML-06-ml3-5-decision-trees-and-interpretable-models-supplemental-3/solution/main.py`.
That reference remains the separate recursive-growth implementation exercise.

The three CSV splits are constructed, fictional two-feature measurements.
The x coordinate determines the authored class rule; y alternates as a
distractor. They contain no personal data or measured external outcomes.

The tree supports two finite numeric features and depths 0 through 8.
Thresholds are midpoints of distinct training values. Route values
`<= threshold` left. Maximize positive Gini reduction, using feature
index then threshold for ties within `1e-12`. Leaves use training
class counts, with alphabetical class ties. The positive-gain rule can
stop on XOR even though a deeper tree could represent XOR.

[Algorithm context](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/tree.html)

# Choose a shallow tree before final evaluation

Use Python 3.10 or later and its standard library. Keep `main.py`,
`exercise.py`, `tree_rules.py` and the `data` folder together:

```sh
python3 main.py --output tree-report.json
```

From another folder, use the absolute path to `main.py`; CSV paths remain
relative to the script. The output path names the report to save.

Complete `choose_depth(scores)` in the starter's `exercise.py`. The
reference completes this task. Select the shallowest candidate whose
validation accuracy is within 0.02 of the best, inclusively with `1e-12`
numerical tolerance. Validate a nonempty dictionary of finite accuracies
from 0 to 1 and integer depths from 0 through 8. Tree construction and
reporting are supplied.

## Worked comparison

The training rows have `x=0` through `7`, alternating `y=0,1`,
and labels A,A,B,B,B,B,A,A. Validation x values 0.5,2.5,4.5,6.5 have labels
A,B,B,A. Depths 0,1,2 score 0.5,0.75,1.0 on validation, selecting depth 2.
A separate map `{1:0.98,2:1.0}` selects depth 1 under the declared
simplicity rule.

The depth-2 tree asks `x<=1.5` at the root, then `x<=5.5` in its
right child. Draw the tree and training counts. Trace test x values
-0.5,1.5,5.5,7.5: predictions A,A,B,A, accuracy 1.0. Training class counts
tie, so the baseline selects A; it scores 0.75 on those same four test rows.

Keep the validation comparison and freeze the chosen fitted tree before
opening test labels. The script fits training rows alone. Changing final-test
labels can change reported accuracy while preserving candidate scores,
chosen depth, fitted counts and predictions.

## Fixed-model probe

Trace `[5.5,0]` and a copy `[5.51,0]`. The first predicts B and the
second A; only the second comparison changes direction. Preserve any
declared true label separately. This measures boundary sensitivity for these
queries, with no new fitting or model selection.

Record the candidate comparison, chosen depth, baseline, one complete path
and the saved JSON report. The tiny fictional fixture demonstrates the
mechanism; its perfect score supplies no evidence about an external population.

"""Select depth from the supplied validation accuracies."""


def choose_depth(scores):
    """Return the shallowest depth within 0.02 of the highest accuracy.

    scores maps integer depths 0 through 8 to finite accuracies from 0 to 1.
    Validate this contract. Treat the 0.02 boundary as inclusive with 1e-12
    numerical tolerance. Use only this mapping; final-test labels are withheld.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("Complete choose_depth(scores).")

ML35-Decision-Tree-Selection/starter/mai.content:
"""Compare fixed tree depths using validation before opening the test split."""
import argparse
from collections import Counter
import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path

from exercise import choose_depth
from tree_rules import fit, predict, trace

DATA = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data"
DEPTHS = (0, 1, 2)


def load_split(name):
    if name not in {"train", "validation", "test"}:
        raise ValueError("Unknown fixed split.")
    with (DATA / (name + ".csv")).open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(handle))
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError("Every split must contain observations.")
    return [[float(row["x"]), float(row["y"])] for row in rows], [
        row["label"] for row in rows
    ]


def accuracy(actual, predicted):
    if not actual or len(actual) != len(predicted):
        raise ValueError("Align nonempty labels and predictions.")
    return sum(a == b for a, b in zip(actual, predicted)) / len(actual)


def select_model(points, labels, validation, validation_labels):
    """No final-test inputs are available during candidate selection."""
    models = {depth: fit(points, labels, depth) for depth in DEPTHS}
    scores = {
        depth: accuracy(validation_labels, [predict(model, row) for row in validation])
        for depth, model in models.items()
    }
    selected = choose_depth(scores.copy())
    if type(selected) is not int or selected not in models:
        raise ValueError("Return one declared integer candidate depth.")
    return selected, models[selected], scores


def experiment():
    points, labels = load_split("train")
    validation, validation_labels = load_split("validation")
    depth, model, scores = select_model(points, labels, validation, validation_labels)
    # Open the reserved split only after the model choice is frozen.
    test, expected = load_split("test")
    predicted = [predict(model, row) for row in test]
    counts = Counter(labels)
    majority = min(counts, key=lambda label: (-counts[label], label))
    return {
        "training_rows": len(points),
        "validation_rows": len(validation),
        "test_rows": len(test),
        "validation_accuracy": scores,
        "selected_depth": depth,
        "selected_tree": model,
        "majority_label": majority,
        "test_predictions": predicted,
        "test_accuracy": accuracy(expected, predicted),
        "baseline_test_accuracy": accuracy(expected, [majority] * len(test)),
        "test_traces": [trace(model, row) for row in test],
    }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, help="Save the complete JSON report.")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    report = json.dumps(experiment(), indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
    if args.output is not None:
        args.output.write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
    print(report, end="")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

coreReading.content:
# Compare shallow trees on fixed observations

The supplied fictional measurements have two features, `x` and `y`,
and class A or B. Training x values are 0 through 7; y alternates 0 and 1.
Labels are A,A,B,B,B,B,A,A. Validation x values 0.5,2.5,4.5,6.5 have labels
A,B,B,A; their y values are 0,1,0,1.

## Worked tree comparison

The root contains four A and four B observations, giving Gini impurity
`1-(4/8)^2-(4/8)^2=1/2`. Splits `x<=1.5` and `x<=5.5` tie
at weighted child impurity 1/3. The supplied rule selects the lower threshold.

At depth 1, the left leaf has two A observations. The right leaf has four B
and two A observations, so it predicts B. At depth 2, the right child splits
at `x<=5.5`, creating a four-B left leaf and two-A right leaf.
The alternating y feature supplies no better split.

Validation predictions and accuracy:

| Depth | Labels | Acc. |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | A,A,A,A | 0.50 |
| 1 | A,B,B,B | 0.75 |
| 2 | A,B,B,A | 1.00 |

Draw the three fitted trees. Trace validation x=6.5 through the depth-2
tree's right and right branches to the A leaf. At depth 1, that query stops
at the mixed B leaf.

## Freeze the comparison

The declared selection rule chooses the shallowest candidate within 0.02
of the best validation accuracy. Here it selects depth 2. Training class
counts tie, so the majority baseline chooses A alphabetically.

Only after freezing the model, open test x values -0.5,1.5,5.5,7.5 with
y values 1,0,1,0 and labels A,A,B,A. The selected tree predicts A,A,B,A,
accuracy 1.0. The training-only baseline predicts A,A,A,A, accuracy 0.75.
Values exactly at a threshold follow the left branch.

The [core project](#machine-learning-ml3-5-decision-trees-and-interpretable-models-curriculum-core-project-5-decision-trees-and-interpretable-models) supplies the complete tree rules and all three
CSV splits. Implement its validation-based selection function and reproduce
the comparison. The separate optional projects develop Gini/split selection
and recursive tree construction. These small fixed observations demonstrate
the mechanism; they support no claim about a wider population.
